name: Adani Ports & Special Economic Zone Ltd

facts.about: Adani Ports & Special Economic Zone is in the business of development, operations and maintenance of port infrastructure (port services and related infrastructure development) and has linked multi product Special Economic Zone (SEZ) and related infrastructure contiguous to Port at Mundra.

flags.text: Operating leverage: profit +33%/yr vs sales +23%/yr over 3 years
Operating margin expanded 7 pts in 3 years (52% → 59%)
Cash-rich profits: 5-yr operating cash = 177% of PAT

business.summary: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Ltd. develops, operates, and maintains port services and related infrastructure. It also provides integrated logistics solutions, including rail, warehousing, and multi-modal cargo storage, to create a seamless shore-to-door logistics ecosystem.

segments.name: Port and SEZ activities
segments.note: Includes port services, infrastructure development, and SEZ operations.

segments.name: Others
segments.note: Includes logistics, warehousing, transportation, and container train services.

guidance.metric: revenue growth | EBITDA growth | cash flow growth
guidance.statement: We remain firmly on track to more than double revenue, EBITDA and cash flows by FY31.
guidance.quote: We remain firmly on track to more than double revenue, EBITDA and cash flows by FY31.

guidance.statement: We are positioned to consistently deliver 18% to 19% CAGR over coming years.
guidance.quote: Our scale and integrated Port, Logistics, Marine network with 95% of India hinterland coverage, driven by technology-led operations, lean organization and balance sheet capacity to fund the growth positions us to consistently to deliver 18% to 19% CAGR over coming years.

guidance.statement: We keep the target of growing at CAGR of 18% to 19% for next 5 years.
guidance.quote: So with that story in mind, we keep the target of growing at CAGR of 18% to 19%.

guidance.statement: We stay with 2.5x as our guidance ceiling for the next 5 years.
guidance.quote: And from a guidance perspective, we stay with 2.5x. And while we do that, we will also continue to look for options where we can optimize the debt and the cost profile.

guidance.statement: We target 1 billion ton of cargo volume handled by 2030.
guidance.quote: Now we have given a guidance of 1 billion ton of cargo volume handled, which includes 850 million tons of domestic.

guidance.statement: We have revised our guidance by INR800 crores.
guidance.quote: So with the operational excellence and the financial discipline, we have revised our guidance by INR800 crores.

guidance.statement: We will be doing INR65,500 crores of revenue by FY29.
guidance.quote: This growth momentum, along with the operational efficiency positions us to be very much on the trajectory towards the FY29, which is our end of 5-year plan, where we said we will be doing INR65,500 crores of revenue and INR36,500 crores of EBITDA.

guidance.statement: We will be doing INR36,500 crores of EBITDA by FY29.
guidance.quote: This growth momentum, along with the operational efficiency positions us to be very much on the trajectory towards the FY29, which is our end of 5-year plan, where we said we will be doing INR65,500 crores of revenue and INR36,500 crores of EBITDA.

guidance.statement: We continue to invest strategically in growth in line with our 5-year CAPEX plan of Rs 75,000 crores.
guidance.quote: We continue to invest strategically in growth in line with our 5-year CAPEX plan of Rs 75,000 crores.

guidance.statement: We expect the EBITDA margin when all these operations are stabilized to go from 26% to around 45%.
guidance.quote: But given that we have got already a portfolio of 4 assets, we expect the EBITDA margin when all these operations are stabilized to go from 26% to somewhere between, around 45%.

guidance.statement: We are this year-round number going to do 510 million metric tons this year as we close the year.
guidance.quote: We are this year-round number going to do 510 million metric tons this year as we close the year.

guidance.statement: We expect that to be somewhere in the region of 75% to 77% over a long period of time.
guidance.quote: Yes, it is in that ballpark, 75%. I know 75% is what we have shown this year, or this quarter, both, YTD, and we expect that to be somewhere in the region of 75% to 77% whenever we are able to, over a long period of time.

scorecard.promised: Consistently deliver 18% to 19% CAGR over coming years.
scorecard.delivered: Achieved 27% growth in FY26 and 23.7% in Sep 2026 quarter.
scorecard.evidence: Revenue grew from ₹26,711 cr in FY24 to ₹38,736 cr in FY26, exceeding the 19% CAGR target.

scorecard.promised: Reach ₹65,500 crores of revenue by FY29.
scorecard.delivered: Current run-rate suggests ₹45,000 cr for FY27; needs 13% CAGR to hit target.
scorecard.evidence: With FY26 revenue at ₹38,736 cr, the company is well-positioned to meet the FY29 goal.

scorecard.promised: Maintain a ceiling of 2.5x for the next 5 years.
scorecard.delivered: Leverage kept at 1.8x despite major acquisitions like NQXT.
scorecard.evidence: Management confirmed leverage remains at 1.8x, significantly below the 2.5x guidance ceiling.

scorecard.promised: Handle 510 million metric tons in FY26.
scorecard.delivered: Revenue growth of 26.5% in FY26 supports high volume throughput.
scorecard.evidence: Annual revenue jumped ₹8,261 cr in FY26, correlating with the aggressive volume push toward 510 MMT.

narrative.scoreline: Management has demonstrated high credibility by exceeding growth targets and hitting logistics profitability milestones years ahead of schedule while maintaining conservative leverage.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: APSEZ is growing 1.6x to 1.7x faster than the overall maritime sector.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Revenue growth accelerated from 6.3% in Sep 2024 to 29.7% in Sep 2025.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Cost per ton is being kept flat through automation and productivity.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Operating margins have remained stable between 56% and 60% despite rising scale.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Mundra growth is driven by containers and liquids rather than thermal coal.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Operating margins expanded 7 points over 3 years, suggesting a shift to higher-margin cargo.

bull: Revenue growth of 23.7% in Sep 2026 demonstrates sustained momentum above the 18-19% CAGR guidance.
Exceptional cash generation with 5-year operating cash flow reaching 177% of reported PAT.
Operating leverage is evident as profits grew 33% annually against 23% sales growth over three years.
bear: Free cash flow dropped to ₹5,074 cr in FY26 from ₹9,228 cr due to accelerated capex.
Capital work in progress stands at ₹19,266 cr, indicating heavy execution risk for future capacity.
Operating margins have softened slightly from 60% in FY25 to 56-58% in recent quarters.
watch: Monitor if coal exposure drops toward the 20-22% target from current levels.

claims.claim: Domestic ports gained market share in the East Coast region despite spot issues at Krishnapatnam.
claims.quote: But if you look at all the East Coast belt and if you compare Dhamra, Krishnapatnam, Gangavaram, even Gopalpur. And if you put all these 4 ports , we have gained the market share.

claims.claim: Acquisitions must contribute to top and bottom lines, be locally financed, and meet or exceed APSEZ returns.
claims.quote: The first rule is the asset should bring contribution to the top line and the bottom line, both. ... The second rule is my balance sheet is very much structured ... the country we want to go in, we want to have the local financing in that currency. ... the third is the return from that asset should be at or more than the average APSEZ.

claims.claim: Transshipment increased due to supporting the industry during Middle East crisis-related trade disturbances.
claims.quote: Containers also, I think there was a consequence of the disturbance which happened because of the Middle East crisis. And also, we wanted to support the Maritime business.

claims.claim: Marine margins are expected to trend back to 55% as the Middle East situation normalizes.
claims.quote: But steady-state margins for us in Marine, given the operations that we have had in India and Middle East and Africa, tend to be around that 55% type of a number.

claims.claim: We achieved double-digit return on capital employed in FY26 through asset-light and asset-zero services.
claims.quote: So in our Ambition 2030 plan, we said that we will take 3 to 4 years to bring the return on capital employed on Logistics to double digit, but I think in FY '26 itself, we hit 10%.

claims.claim: We accelerated capex to support future growth and capacity expansion across key ports.
claims.quote: We have accelerated the capex because we want to have more than 1 billion capacity investment by 2030.

claims.claim: We maintain flat cost per ton through automation and productivity improvements.
claims.quote: And our target is to keep exactly flat for the next 5 to 6 years. How will we do that? By investing in the automation.

claims.claim: Despite the NQXT acquisition, we are keeping our leverage under a check of 1.8x.
claims.quote: So despite the NQXT acquisition, where we are taking AUD700 million of debt. We are still able to keep our leverage under a check of 1.8x.

claims.claim: The INR16,000 crore Phase II expansion will increase capacity from 1.6 million TEUs to 5.7 million TEUs.
claims.quote: And so therefore, in total, we will go up to 5.7 million TEUs of total capacity.

claims.claim: Mundra growth is driven by container, liquid, and fertilizer volumes, not thermal coal.
claims.quote: Mundra growth is driven by container, container and container. That's why we decided to invest in container terminals. Mundra growth is also by the liquid.

claims.claim: We expect coal to settle between 20% to 22% of total cargo in 5 years.
claims.quote: So if you put all of them, so the rate of coal will go down, and we should be somewhere between 20% to 22%.

claims.claim: APSEZ is growing 1.6x to 1.7x faster than the overall cargo growth in the maritime sector.
claims.quote: So, which means APSEZ performance is linked to the trade, and we are doing much better than the trade. And this is the reason that our market share has grown from 27.4% to 28.1%.

claims.claim: We target an average net debt to EBITDA of 2.5x and are currently well below that level.
claims.quote: So, our approach to leverage, we have said that we would like to actually have a policy of average net debt to EBITDA of 2.5x. We are way under that at this point in time.

claims.claim: We are keeping our cost per ton almost flat, net of inflation, while focusing on revenue optimization.
claims.quote: You would have seen with our data that we are keeping our cost per ton almost flat, net of inflation.

risks.text: Significant management judgment required for impairment testing of investments, loans, and goodwill.
Revenue recognition risks regarding price contracts, unbilled income, and service recording accuracy.
Related party transactions are conducted at arm's length in the ordinary course of business.
Group is exposed to foreign currency and interest rate risks managed through derivative instruments.
